title: Active Regression for Single-Index Models with Unknown Link Functions
abstract:
This paper studies active regression for single-index models under general $\ell_p$-loss with an unknown $1$-Lipschitz link function $f$, formulated as $\min_{f,x} \Vert f(Ax)-b\Vert_p^p$ with full access to $A$ but coordinate-query access to $b$. 
Prior work established upper bounds for known link functions for all $p\geq 1$ and for unknown link functions only in the $p=2$ case, together with lower bounds for $p\leq 2$.
This work addresses the more challenging setting of unknown link functions and general $p \geq 1$.
A non-adaptive sampling algorithm is presented that achieves a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation using $O(d^{p/2\vee 1}/\epsilon^{p\vee 2}\text{poly}\log(n/\epsilon))$ queries. Nearly tight lower bounds are also established for non-adaptive queries when $p>2$. These results close much of the remaining gap in active $\ell_p$ regression for single-index models.
problem: Active regression for single-index models with unknown Lipschitz link functions under general p-norm loss remains challenging.
approach: Present non-adaptive sampling algorithm achieving (1+epsilon)-approximation with query complexity O(d^(p/2 v 1) / epsilon^(p v 2) polylog(n/epsilon)); establish nearly tight lower bounds for p>2.
contribution: Closes remaining gaps in active ell-p regression theory for single-index models with unknown link functions.
